items.name: Verdict row
items.probe_answer_excerpt: Of 134 rows only 1 is complete: 11 lack sha, 64 lack exit and sha, 58 lack all three... When it is missing the row is a report, not a verdict, and the gate never saw it... a settle with nothing recorded derives no-verdict.
items.rubric_truth: A row {command, exitCode, sha} recorded via orchestration_verdict bound to the execution head sha; most closed cards lack one because the ritual was adopted after they ran (0.99% / 4 of 897); missing row => gate derives FAIL no-verdict no-sha regardless of delivered work.
items.source_that_settles_it: orchestration/VERDICTS.md:4166-4173, :4216-4233; the orchestration_verdict contract; measured adoption 4/897 = 0.99%
items.why: Mechanism and the 'report, not a verdict' ruling are right, but it never writes the derived verdict word FAIL and gives a row-completeness count (1 of 134) rather than the adoption figure (4 of 897 closures), and its cause is 'handoffs recorded prose', not the ritual being adopted after most cards ran. Right answer with the decisive consequence unstated.
